rationale: All candidates are near-clones for the target (same PheCode 411.3 angina pectoris endpoint, same MVP development cohort, same basic covariates age/sex/20 PCs, same validation ancestry and n=30,750), and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we must rely on within-family performance proxies. PGS005048 has the highest reported full-model C-index/AUC (0.76688) among the shortlist with otherwise identical covariate packaging, giving it the best available discrimination signal versus the closest runner-up PGS005052 (0.76625). Effect sizes are all similar (OR ~1.45–1.49), with no materially stronger alternative that would justify overriding the upstream top rank.

PGS002786 is the only candidate whose trait_reported/trait_efo directly matches the target trait (bipolar disorder), whereas PGS002787 and PGS002788 are subtype-specific (bipolar I / bipolar II). All three are otherwise near-clones (same publication, SDPR method, PGC training cohort, EUR-only GWAS/EVAL, similar variant counts, and only small full-model partial R² values with basic covariates). Although PGS002788 has the highest reported partial R², these are full-model partial R² values on non-disease phenotyping endpoints and are very close in magnitude, so they are weak tie-breakers; endpoint/label fidelity therefore keeps the upstream top-ranked direct bipolar disorder model (PGS002786) as the best-supported match.

PGS001033 is the only candidate mapped to the broad target EFO (blood coagulation disease) and it provides clean PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC no covariates 0.634; PGS R² no covariates 0.0578) with only basic covariates, making it the best-supported direct match on comparable metrics. The main runner-up (PGS002034; near-clone with PGS001826) targets a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency EFO and reports only partial correlation (~0.056) without PRS-only AUROC/R², so it has weaker directly comparable discrimination evidence despite a larger variant set.

PGS002738 is the best direct match to the target (trait_efo=alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported=Alcohol use disorder) and shows the strongest available discrimination proxy among the alcohol-dependence–aligned candidates: OR(top 10% vs rest)=1.96 (1.54–2.51), exceeding the closest runner-up PGS002739 (OR=1.76). It is also a genome-wide PRS-CS score with substantial variant count (326k) and is developed from major cohorts (MVP, UKB) with a reasonably sized EUR validation (n=7,900). In contrast, PGS000201/PGS000202 are for ‘problematic alcohol use’ (trait_efo=alcohol dependence measurement) rather than dependence/AUD itself and only report small incremental ΔR² (0.0119 and 0.0046), making them weaker direct-match candidates despite cleaner covariate disclosure.

PGS001263 is the only candidate with an exact atrial flutter endpoint across trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, and it provides clean PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.617, PGS R2=0.025) with basic covariates and a multi-ancestry evaluation set. The strongest runner-up is PGS001339 (same snpnet/UKB framework family and similarly clean PRS-only metrics), but it targets a combined AF+flutter time-to-event phenotype and has slightly weaker PRS-only performance (AUROC 0.613, R2 0.024). The other two (PGS002050, PGS001841) are also AF+flutter composites and report only partial-r (no PRS-only AUC/R2), making them less directly comparable for PRS benchmarking despite larger variant counts/training N.

All candidates are direct asthma matches, but PGS001344 has the cleanest and strongest PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.64568 and PGS-only R2=0.05973 (no covariates), plus incremental AUROC=0.07977, giving a clearer standalone-PRS signal than the others. The strongest runner-up is PGS001782 (same trait, PRS-CS-auto) which reports covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.048844 and AUROC=0.659, but it comes from a global biobank framework paper and has smaller validation (n=7,128) than PGS001344’s UKB evaluation (n=19,857). PGS002727 is pediatric-specific (endpoint restriction) and only shows full-model AUROC (0.66) with unknown covariates, while PGS002061 reports only partial-r (0.1184) without PRS-only AUC/R2. PGS001344’s PRS-only metrics are also below the asthma liability h2 ceiling (~0.1515), supporting metric plausibility.

PGS001268 and PGS001267 are near-clones from the same UKB snpnet study family with the same ancestry setup, covariates, variant count (10), and validation size, so their PRS-only metrics are directly comparable. PGS001268 has consistently stronger PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC 0.7346 vs 0.7265; PGS R2 0.1023 vs 0.0988) and slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.7488 vs 0.7433), while remaining within the heritability ceiling sanity check. The top-ranked portability candidates (PGS002089/PGS001876) lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and only report weaker partial-r (0.0919/0.0797), and PGS003420’s higher full-model AUROC is based on a small EAS-only validation (n=1,298) with unknown covariates and no PRS-only metrics, making it less reliable for benchmark-leading selection.

PGS000327 is the cleaner direct-match for autism spectrum disorder: its phenotyping_reported is explicitly “Autism spectrum disorder” (endpoint-faithful), whereas PGS002790’s phenotyping_reported is “Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)”, indicating an endpoint mismatch despite the ASD trait label. On performance proxies, PGS000327 shows stronger evidence (full-model R²=0.0245 and OR=1.33 per SD with tight CI) versus PGS002790’s weaker partial R²=0.00546 and no effect-size reporting. Both are EUR-evaluated with basic PC-style covariates, but PGS000327 also has clearer disease-focused multi-cohort development and larger validation (n=7,148 vs n=2,198), reinforcing it as the best-supported candidate.

All candidates are near-clones for endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to breast cancer/breast carcinoma), come from the same publication, have the same training cohort (UKB), similar EUR-focused ancestry context, identical stated covariates (0), and the same validation sample size (n=48,968), so performance/effect-size differences are the main differentiator. PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) has the strongest reported validation signals among the set: highest full-model AUROC (0.6625 vs 0.6598 for the closest runner-up PGS004040) and highest R² (0.0764 vs 0.0739), plus the largest per-SD effect size (OR 1.826 vs 1.809). Given the same-study near-clone context and the additional structural advantage of being an ensemble/multi-PRS model, PGS004153 is the best-supported pick over the strongest runner-up (PGS004040).

ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency
rationale: Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB portability paper with identical trait/phenotyping, training cohort (UKB), covariates, ancestry distribution, and validation size; neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, and their partial-r is essentially identical (0.0563 vs 0.0562), so performance evidence does not differentiate. With metrics tied, the main structural advantage is method/coverage: PGS002034 uses LDpred2 with genome-wide shrinkage and far more variants (32,552 vs 45), which is generally favored for capturing polygenic signal when endpoints and evaluation context are the same. Therefore PGS002034 is the best-supported pick over PGS001826.

All candidates are direct matches for basal cell carcinoma with identical basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4) and EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL, so endpoint fidelity and leakage risk do not differentiate. Within the near-clone MGI-developed cluster (PGS000452/454/456/458; same training n=11,734 and validation n=11,322), PGS000454 has the strongest overall performance signals: it ties for best full-model AUROC (0.632, same as PGS000452) while having the highest Nagelkerke R² (0.0489 vs 0.0487 for PGS000452 and ~0.0456–0.0457 for PGS000456/458) and a slightly stronger top-1% vs rest OR (3.79 vs 3.61). The UKB-developed PGS000457 has much larger training/validation but clearly weaker discrimination (AUROC 0.617, R² 0.0322, OR per SD 1.535), so it is not competitive despite scale. Given the near-identical design among the MGI siblings, the small but consistent metric edge makes PGS000454 the best-supported pick.

All candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm, but PGS003973 and PGS003972 come from the same disease-focused Nat Genet AAA meta-analysis and use the same PRS-CS genome-wide approach (~1.12M variants), making them the strongest study-family cluster versus the framework/portability scores (PGS001784, PGS002054) and the older sparse P+T score (PGS000753). Between the two Nat Genet siblings, PGS003973 has cleaner disclosed basic covariates (age, age^2, sex) and reports a higher discrimination metric (C-index 0.882 with tight CI) than PGS003972’s AUROC 0.69 with unknown covariates, so it has the clearer within-family performance signal. The very high full-model metric is interpreted cautiously (not PRS-only), but given the near-clone context it is still the best available tie-break among the top disease-focused candidates.

PGS001135 is the only candidate that is a direct match to the target trait at the EFO level (arthritis) and also provides clean PRS-only performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.539 and PGS-only R²=0.00291) with basic covariates and a multi-ancestry evaluation context. The strongest runner-up for the same arthritis EFO is PGS004547 (and sibling PGS004477), but both come from a risk-factor integration study with unknown covariates and provide only a modest per-SD OR (1.26 / 1.20) and no AUC/R², making their standalone PRS performance less well-supported/comparable here. The osteoarthritis-specific scores (PGS001290, PGS001192) are endpoint-mismatched to generic arthritis despite having metrics, so they are weaker direct matches.

PGS005252 is the strongest direct-match package for aortic stenosis: it has exact trait/EFO alignment and an explicit incident aortic stenosis endpoint, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDPred2) with very high variant count (~1.12M), and reports the strongest available PRS signal among the direct AS candidates (HR=1.92 per SD) plus a high C-index/full-model AUC (0.87) in a very large European validation (n=446,895). The closest runner-up is PGS005254, which is also endpoint-faithful and cleaner on covariates (age/sex/PCs only) with larger training (n=205,483), but it provides no discrimination metric and shows a materially weaker effect size (HR=1.64). PGS005255/PGS005256 are less directly aligned (valve-function traits) and also have weaker HR (~1.53). PGS000739 is for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and is not a direct match.

All candidates are endpoint-faithful to major depressive disorder, but four (PGS003578/PGS003580/PGS003576/PGS003584) are near-clone siblings from the same MDD phenotype-integration study with the same ancestry setup and covariates (PCs 1–10). Within that comparable family, PGS003578 has the strongest reported validation performance (full-model R²=0.0257 vs 0.0254/0.0241/0.0207), making it the best-supported pick among the most directly comparable options. The higher-ranked PGS003333 is from a different EHR/PheWAS-oriented paper with unknown covariates and EUR-only evaluation, and it shows weaker reported R² (Nagelkerke pseudo-R²=0.022) despite using a shrinkage method, so it lacks a clear multi-field advantage over the best-performing near-clone sibling.

All candidates are broadly aligned to celiac disease, but PGS000040 is the most disease-focused direct endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Coeliac disease) with the strongest reported discrimination among the direct-disease models (full-model AUROC=0.90). The main runner-up is PGS001301, which has clean PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC(no covariates)=0.8287; PGS R2=0.1422) but comes from a pan-trait UKB framework phenotype (“Malabsorption/coeliac disease”), a study archetype that domain guidance flags as less reliable for external transfer than disease-focused models unless it has a clear multi-field advantage. The HLA-DQ2.5-carrier–restricted scores (PGS000041/PGS000042) are endpoint-restricted and also show materially lower AUROC (~0.72–0.73), and PGS000316 has lower AUROC (0.879) despite very large evaluation N and a small-variant GRS. Given the shortlist, PGS000040 best balances endpoint fidelity with the strongest visible performance proxy among the disease-specific candidates.

PGS002755 is the strongest direct-match for generic atopic eczema/dermatitis risk in this shortlist: it targets incident atopic dermatitis (aligned to atopic eczema), is evaluated in a very large European cohort (n=337,910), and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS) with ~1.09M variants—structurally better for a polygenic disease than the sparse GWAS-hit scores here. The closest runner-up is PGS004587, which shares the same incident endpoint and validation setting but is only 23 genome-wide significant SNPs and shows a weaker HR (1.153 vs 1.249 high-vs-low PRS), suggesting less captured polygenic signal. PGS001773’s very high full-model AUROC/R² comes from a small Canadian cohort (n=676) and a different severity-defined endpoint (moderate-to-severe), making it less reliable/transferable for general atopic eczema risk; PGS003459/PGS003486 are therapy-context ‘paradoxical eczema’ in biologic-treated psoriasis, an endpoint mismatch for generic atopic eczema.

PGS005170 is the strongest direct match for the target trait dementia on endpoint fidelity and study archetype: it is explicitly "All-cause dementia" with "Incident all-cause dementia" phenotyping and comes from a dementia-focused integrative PRS study (ensemble of 24 component PRSs; 1,320,229 variants) with multi-ancestry evaluation reported. The main runner-up is PGS004281, which also targets all-cause dementia and shows a higher full-model AUROC (~0.819), but it is a single-UKB method paper score with only full-model metrics (no PRS-only AUC/R2) and thus its apparent advantage is more likely covariate-driven and less reliable for external benchmark transfer. PGS000929 provides clean PRS-only AUC/R2, but it is a sparse pan-trait UKB framework score ("813 traits"), a known weaker archetype for external generalization versus a disease-focused integrative dementia model. Overall, PGS005170 has the best-supported, disease-focused evidence package despite lacking PRS-only metrics.

All three candidates are direct Crohn’s disease matches by trait_efo/phenotyping. PGS004254 has a clear multi-field advantage over the strongest runner-up (PGS001331): it is not from the pan-trait UKB “813 traits” sparse snpnet framework (a known underperforming archetype for external transfer), uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2-auto) with vastly broader variant coverage (744,682 vs 257), and reports strong PRS effect-size evidence (OR 2.18 per SD, 95% CI 2.05–2.32), indicating materially stronger discrimination than the modest PRS-only AUROC/R2 in PGS001331 (PGS-only AUROC ~0.58; R2 ~0.0068). Although PGS004254 lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2 (only a full-model AUROC 0.72 with basic covariates), the combination of endpoint fidelity, method/coverage, and strong OR support outweighs the small PRS-only metric edge of the sparse framework scores. Between the two snpnet siblings, PGS001331 is slightly better than PGS001330, but both remain weaker than PGS004254 on structural and effect-size evidence.

All candidates are direct matches for atrial fibrillation, so the decision turns on performance proxies, covariate comparability, and study/transport context. PGS005168’s very high C-index (0.8718) is heavily discounted because its covariates explicitly include the CHARGE-AF clinical risk calculator (risk-wrapper packaging), making the full-model metric largely non-comparable to standalone PRS performance. Versus that, PGS005313 reports strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.82, tight CI) with only basic covariates (age, sex) and is built with a cross-ancestry PRS-CSx approach and evaluated in a multi-ancestry setting, which is supportive for external benchmark transfer. The main runner-up is PGS005168 due to its large disease-focused meta-analysis context, but the CHARGE-AF packaging undermines its apparent metric advantage; PGS005313 is the cleaner, better-supported PRS candidate on the visible evidence.

All candidates are direct matches to cervical carcinoma and use incident/disease endpoints, but PGS003428 is the only clearly disease-focused, cervical-phenotype GWAS meta-analysis score using a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with very large variant coverage (~2.9M) and multi-cohort development (EB, FinnGen, KP, UKB), which is a stronger structural and study-archetype signal for external PRS performance than the sparse GWAS-hit portability-style scores. The strongest runner-up is PGS000073 (and its near-clone PGS000784), which shows a much higher reported full-model AUROC (~0.745) but that metric is not PRS-only and is paired with a heavier covariate bundle (parity, oral contraceptive use, pack-years, etc.), making the apparent discrimination less attributable to the PRS itself; additionally these are 10-variant GWS scores likely capturing less polygenic signal than the LDpred genome-wide model. PGS003428 also reports a moderate per-SD HR (1.33), supporting non-trivial PRS signal despite only a modest full-model C-index (0.613).

All candidates are direct COPD matches, but PGS001783 has the strongest PRS-comparable performance evidence: a covariates-regressed-out (PRS-only) Nagelkerke R2 of 0.038092, which is materially higher than the closest same-publication sibling PGS001788 (PRS-only R2=0.0163) and far higher than the UKB sparse snpnet framework scores (PGS001332/333/334; PRS-only R2≈0.00235–0.00314, AUROC(no-covars)≈0.54–0.55). The R2 for PGS001783 is also plausible under the provided COPD heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.0388), supporting metric sanity. Between the two Global Biobank PRS-CS-auto candidates, endpoint and evaluation ancestry are the same (COPD; EUR eval), so the clear PRS-only R2 advantage makes PGS001783 the best-supported pick despite its smaller listed validation n.

PGS004621 is the strongest direct match to the target (trait_efo=cirrhosis of liver; phenotyping_reported=Cirrhosis) while also having the most robust structural and study-support signals: a genome-wide PRS-CS model with ~1.09M variants and development across many large biobanks (AllofUs, FinnGen, UKB, deCODE, etc.), plus very large European evaluation (n=1,153,995). Against the closest runner-up PGS000726 (also cirrhosis of liver), PGS004621 has a much more polygenic genome-wide construction (vs 12 GWAS hits) and far broader multi-cohort backing; although both lack PRS-only AUC/R2, PGS004621’s evidence package is more consistent with stronger external benchmark performance. The other candidates are weaker due to endpoint mismatch toward alcoholic cirrhosis/time-to-event packaging (PGS000704, PGS000776, PGS001777) and/or much smaller or sparser score construction.

All candidates are direct CAD matches, but PGS003725 is the strongest within the top-ranked Nat Med 2023 multi-ancestry LDpred2 sibling cluster: it has the highest reported effect sizes (HR 1.75 and OR 2.14 per SD) versus PGS003726 (HR 1.73 only) and PGS003727 (HR 1.67), with essentially identical basic covariates (age/sex/PCs) and the same large validation size (n=308,264). Compared with the main non-sibling runner-up PGS002244 (Cell Genom 2022 LDpred), PGS003725 shows materially stronger discrimination proxy via effect size (OR 2.14 vs 1.64) while retaining comparable endpoint fidelity and broad multi-ancestry evaluation, making it the best-supported choice despite the absence of PRS-only AUC/R2 across the shortlist.

All candidates are direct matches to dilated cardiomyopathy, but PGS004949 has the strongest PRS-specific performance evidence among the MTAG Nat Genet 2024 siblings: it reports the highest univariate (PRS-only) AUC (0.68, 95% CI 0.66–0.69) and a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.91), with only basic demographic/PC/array covariates. The closest runner-up is PGS004951, which is similarly endpoint-faithful (clinical DCM) and has slightly higher OR (1.93) but lower PRS-only AUC (0.67) and much smaller validation sample (n=7,761 vs n=326,106). The higher full-model AUROC in PGS004862/PGS004861 is less decisive because it is not PRS-only and those models lack explicit PRS-only metrics, making them weaker for benchmark-oriented comparison versus PGS004949’s clean PRS-only AUC.

PGS004546 is the most endpoint-faithful direct match (ICD10 K80 cholelithiasis; trait_efo cholelithiasis) and, within its same-publication near-clone pair (PGS004546 vs PGS004476), it has a materially stronger per-SD effect size (OR 1.299 vs 1.219) while sharing the same training cohort (UKB), training N (174,489), variant count (~1.06M), EUR-only development/evaluation, and validation N (56,192). The main alternative with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS001174) comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (snpnet, 970 variants) and uses a time-to-event phenotype; despite reporting PGS-only AUROC/R2 (0.623/0.028), that framework archetype and endpoint framing are weaker external-performance proxies than the newer disease-focused K80 score family, and its PRS-only R2 remains modest relative to the trait’s heritability ceiling. PGS002072/PGS001861 are portability-framework composites (cholelithiasis+cholecystitis) with only partial-r reported and no clearer PRS-only discrimination advantage over the K80-focused 2024 models.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB portability paper with identical trait/phenotyping (corneal dystrophy), covariates, training cohort/size, ancestry distribution, and validation sample size, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2. The main differentiators are the selected validation metric and model structure: PGS002042 shows higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0471 vs 0.0384 for PGS001835) with overlapping but higher point estimate, and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (59,944 vs 38), which is a positive structural signal when endpoints are identical. Therefore PGS002042 has the clearer multi-field advantage over the strongest runner-up (PGS001835).

PGS002237 is the strongest overall direct-match package: it is explicitly CKD stage 3+ with a clear phenotyping definition (eGFR <45), very large training scale (UKB n=279,819), and—critically—was developed/evaluated across multiple ancestries (EVAL includes AFR/AMR/ASN/EUR/MAE), which is a robust transportability signal for a generic “chronic kidney disease” target. Its reported effect size is also the strongest in the shortlist (OR 1.47 per SD) among broadly comparable CKD endpoints. The main runner-up is PGS005090, which shows a higher full-model AUROC (0.90) and reports R²=0.10, but it is AFR-only GWAS/EVAL and the AUROC/R² are not labeled PRS-only and are therefore likely covariate-influenced (age/sex/diabetes/PCs), making the apparent metric edge less comparable; additionally, its training sample size is not provided. Other candidates either have weaker effect sizes (PGS002757 OR 1.15), more endpoint restriction/packaging (PGS004889 incident CKD without diabetes with a clinical risk score), or lack performance metrics and are more ancillary-study framed (PGS005113).

PGS004913 is the most endpoint-faithful, disease-focused direct match: trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are explicitly alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis, with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs) and a dedicated study in heavy drinkers. While it lacks PRS-only AUC/R2, it provides PRS signal via R²=0.029 and a strong top-vs-bottom decile OR=4.4 in EUR validation (n=3,360). The strongest runner-up is PGS001777, which shows a higher extreme-group OR (6.18) but is a very sparse 3-variant score with unknown covariates and a full-model AUROC (0.671) that is not PRS-comparable; its phenotyping_reported also appears narrower/sex-specific ('Cirrhosis (males)'). PGS000704 has large-scale UKB development and a slightly higher full-model C-index (0.711) but comes from a broad framework-style paper and shows only modest per-SD HR=1.18, making it less compelling as a standalone PRS for this specific endpoint than the dedicated cirrhosis-in-heavy-drinkers score.

All three are broadly aligned to bilirubin metabolism disease, but PGS002032 and PGS001824 are the cleanest direct matches (phenotyping_reported/trait_reported both exactly “Disorders of bilirubin excretion”), whereas PGS000924 is a broader composite and time-to-event endpoint (“TTE disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism”) spanning two EFO traits. Between the two near-clone direct-match portability scores (same publication, same training cohort/size, same covariates, same evaluation setup, and identical partial-r=0.0716), PGS002032 has a clear structural advantage via a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (19,768 vs 22), which is the most meaningful differentiator available given identical reported performance. PGS000924 reports strong PRS-only AUROC/R2, but it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework and its PRS-only R2 (0.218) is implausibly above the provided local h2_obs ceiling (~0.089), making its metric evidence suspect despite the clean formatting.

PGS000639 is the strongest direct-match within the coherent Cancer PRSweb Hodgkin’s disease cluster: it has consistent endpoint alignment (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both Hodgkin’s disease; trait_efo Hodgkins lymphoma), clean/basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs), and the best available performance proxies among the near-clone siblings (highest full-model AUROC 0.62 and highest Nagelkerke R² 0.0276, plus the strongest per-SD effect size OR 1.476). The closest runner-up is PGS000638 (same study/endpoint/covariates/ancestry) but it is uniformly weaker on AUROC (0.601), R² (0.0193), and OR (1.377). PGS003449 is deprioritized despite large validation N because its phenotyping_reported is explicitly mismatched (Chronic lymphocytic leukemia) and it shows a near-null OR (~1.02), making it a poor direct-match signal for Hodgkin lymphoma.

All three candidates are near-clones from the same preprint, with identical endpoint alignment to the target (trait_efo Hashimoto's thyroiditis; phenotyping_reported lymphocytic thyroiditis) and the same evaluation setting (MAE 100%, n=94,651; covariates unknown), and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2—so full-model AUROC differences are weak tie-breakers. Between the strongest alternatives, PGS005270 has a slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.639 vs 0.630) but shows essentially no PRS signal by effect size (OR≈1.04), whereas PGS005271 shows a much stronger per-SD effect (OR≈1.55), which is a more informative proxy for standalone PRS discrimination when PRS-only metrics are absent. PGS005272 is weaker on both AUROC (0.605) and effect size (OR≈1.42) than PGS005271. Therefore PGS005271 is the best-supported direct-match candidate.

PGS001792 is the strongest direct-match because it combines clean PRS-comparable performance evidence with good endpoint fidelity. It targets primary open-angle glaucoma (phenotyping_reported matches) and reports a covariates-regressed-out PRS metric (Nagelkerke R2 / pgs_only_r2=0.03209), which is interpretable as PRS signal and is below the glaucoma liability h2 ceiling (0.0556). The closest runner-up is PGS004944 (also POAG, large validation, strong OR=1.74), but it lacks any PRS-only metric and only provides a full-model AUROC (0.748), making its discrimination harder to attribute to the PRS despite basic covariates. Between the two near-clone Global Biobank scores, PGS001792 edges PGS001797 by slightly higher PRS-only R2 (0.03209 vs 0.031479) and much larger validation sample (347,396 vs 7,128), supporting more stable benchmarking.

All three candidates are direct matches to Dupuytren contracture (same EFO; highly consistent trait_reported/phenotyping). Between the two strongest contenders, PGS002092 and PGS001880 are near-clones from the same UKB portability paper with identical training cohort (UKB), training N, covariates, and multi-ancestry evaluation; the only visible differentiator is performance, where PGS002092 has slightly higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0797 vs 0.0783). PGS001254 reports clean PRS-only AUROC/R2, but it comes from the pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“813 traits”) with only 11 variants, which is a known weaker archetype for external benchmark performance versus genome-wide shrinkage/penalized models; its PRS-only AUROC (0.6646) does not clearly outweigh that structural disadvantage. Therefore the top-ranked, genome-wide LDpred2 score PGS002092 is the best-supported pick over the close sibling PGS001880.

PGS002304 is the strongest direct-match on endpoint fidelity and the only candidate with coherent follicular-lymphoma labeling across trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, whereas the closest runner-up by label (PGS003455) has an explicit phenotyping mismatch (phenotyping_reported = chronic lymphocytic leukemia) that undermines endpoint validity despite large validation N. Against the PRSweb nodular-lymphoma scores (PGS000644/PGS000643), PGS002304 shows materially better reported discrimination in the selected European validation (full-model AUROC 0.61 vs ~0.53–0.54) and comes from a multi-cohort cancer evaluation context rather than a single-cohort development/evaluation setup; although it is a sparse GWAS-hits score (6 variants) with unknown covariates and small validation n, it remains the best-supported follicular-lymphoma-specific candidate in this shortlist given the endpoint incoherence of PGS003455 and weaker performance of the PRSweb alternatives.

PGS000078 and PGS000789 are near-clones: same 109-variant lung cancer score, same EUR-only evaluation, same incident lung cancer endpoint, same very covariate-heavy risk-factor package (family history, detailed smoking variables/interactions, PM2.5), and essentially identical full-model AUROC/C-index (~0.846/0.849) with similar HR per SD (~1.16–1.17). With no PRS-only AUC/R2 available for any candidate, the small differences between these siblings are not meaningful; the upstream-ranked original score (PGS000078) is therefore preferred. PGS004860 reports a higher full-model AUROC (0.893) but comes from a much smaller single cohort (n=24,012) and its full-model metric is not PRS-comparable; PGS000740 is an early-onset (<50) endpoint mismatch; PGS000721 has substantially weaker discrimination (AUROC 0.738) and tiny validation (n=1,202).

All candidates are direct gout matches (trait_reported/efo/phenotyping all ‘Gout’), so the decision turns on the strongest comparable performance evidence without obvious covariate leakage. PGS004160 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) has the best reported discrimination within the well-matched AJHG five-biobank cluster: highest full-model AUROC (0.694 vs 0.685 for PGS004047 and 0.678 for PGS004018) and strongest effect size (OR per SD 2.05 vs 2.00 and 1.93), with covariates listed as ‘0’ (clean/no added clinical predictors) and large validation (n=90,274; EUR/SAS). The higher-ranked Cell Genomics scores (PGS004768/PGS004767) only report incremental R2 (0.081/0.061) from a covariate-adjusted framework and provide no AUROC/effect-size evidence, making them less benchmark-informative here despite larger training N.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB portability paper with identical trait/phenotyping (“Disorders of iron metabolism”), covariates, training N, ancestry evaluation mix, and validation sample size, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2. In this like-for-like setting, PGS002031 has a small but consistent edge in the selected European validation partial correlation (partial-r 0.1355 vs 0.1307) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with substantially more variants (6713 vs 654), which is a favorable structural signal when endpoints and evaluation context are otherwise the same. The advantage is modest, hence moderate confidence.

PGS000114 is the only candidate that directly matches the target umbrella trait (juvenile idiopathic arthritis) across trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, whereas PGS000324/PGS000325/PGS000326 are subtype-specific endpoints (enthesitis-related, oligoarticular, RF-negative polyarticular). All four are from the same disease-focused publication, use the same method (SparSNP), same basic covariates (sex, PCs 1–10), and EUR-only dev/eval, and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2—so subtype full-model AUROC differences (e.g., 0.93 for PGS000324) are not sufficient to override the clear endpoint-fidelity advantage for the broad target. Versus the strongest runner-up (PGS000324), PGS000114 sacrifices a higher full-model AUROC but avoids a subtype mismatch, making it the best-supported direct-match for generic JIA.

PGS004236 is the strongest direct-match hypertension candidate because it comes from a disease-focused, multi-ethnic hypertension study (Nat Commun) with explicit evidence of strong PRS signal (OR=2.1 per SD, 95% CI 1.99–2.21) and broad multi-ancestry evaluation context, suggesting better real-world transfer than UKB-only framework scores. The main runner-up is PGS001320, which uniquely reports clean PRS-only AUROC/R² (PGS-only AUROC=0.629; R²=0.0649) but is from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework (“across 813 traits”), a study archetype noted to generalize less well externally despite tidy metrics. Between the two near-direct matches, the combination of disease-focused design plus strong effect-size evidence favors PGS004236 over the framework-derived PGS001320; PGS004234 is a near-clone of PGS004236 but slightly weaker on full-model AUROC (0.763 vs 0.764) and lacks the strong OR field shown for PGS004236.

PGS004908 is the strongest direct-match package in this shortlist: it targets kidney cancer/renal carcinoma with coherent phenotyping (“Kidney cancer”), comes from a large disease-focused multi-ancestry GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet; BBJ/FinnGen/NCI), and shows the strongest available PRS signal via effect size (OR per SD 1.50, 95% CI 1.43–1.58). Although only a full-model AUROC is reported (0.74) and covariates include standard epidemiologic factors (age/sex/PCs plus BMI/smoking/hypertension), the effect-size strength and modern, well-powered disease-GWAS basis outweigh the older cross-cancer near-clone runner-up PGS000076/PGS000787, which use only 19 variants and show weaker HR per SD (~1.15–1.16) with similar full-model AUROC (~0.722). The other candidates (PGS000722, PGS004690) have materially lower full-model AUROC (~0.56) and no compensating PRS-only metrics or effect sizes.

PGS002763 is the strongest direct-match hip osteoarthritis PRS in this shortlist: it has exact endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported="Hip osteoarthritis" vs PGS002728 using the treatment/proxy endpoint "Total hip replacement"), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with ~1.05M variants, and reports a solid per-SD effect size (OR=1.38, 95% CI 1.31–1.46) under basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/technical). The main runner-up is PGS002728, which is disease-focused and reports a full-model AUROC=0.66, but that metric is not PRS-only and is tied to a proxy surgical endpoint with only age/sex covariates, making it less directly comparable to hip OA risk. PGS000967 provides clean PRS-only AUROC/R2 but comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (snpnet, 634 variants) with weak PRS-only discrimination (AUROC 0.561; R2 0.0063), which is unlikely to beat a disease-focused genome-wide score. The 2024 Commun Biol scores (PGS004478/PGS004548) have coherent ICD framing but lack covariate and discrimination details here and show weaker ORs than PGS002763.

PGS004614 is the most disease-focused, endpoint-faithful candidate (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both “Diverticular disease”) from a dedicated diverticular-disease GWAS paper, using a genome-wide shrinkage method (SBayesR) with very large variant coverage (~1.08M) and evaluated across multiple ancestries. The strongest runner-up is PGS000997 because it reports clean PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.591; R2 0.0178) and has basic covariates, but it comes from a pan-trait UKB sparse-score framework (“across 813 traits”) that is penalized for weaker external generalization; its PRS-only performance is only modest and consistent with the low heritability ceiling. PGS004614’s reported AUROC (0.76) is full-model and includes family history (so not PRS-comparable), which lowers confidence, but overall its disease-specific study archetype + genome-wide construction and direct phenotype alignment outweigh the framework-score advantage of PGS000997’s cleaner metric fields.

PGS005268 and PGS005269 are near-clone siblings from the same multi-biobank, multi-ancestry study with the same hypothyroidism endpoint and identical evaluation sample size (n=94,651) and ancestry framing, so their reported metrics/effect sizes are directly comparable. Between them, PGS005268 has a (slightly) higher full-model AUROC (0.6389209 vs 0.6386285) and marginally stronger effect sizes (OR 1.6581 vs 1.6521; β 0.5057 vs 0.5020), making it the better-supported pick within that matched context. Although PGS005218 shows a much higher AUROC (0.859), it is explicitly covariate-heavy with near-outcome thyroid biomarkers (TSH, T4, anti-TPO), so that full-model AUROC is likely dominated by clinical covariates and is not comparable evidence of standalone PRS quality; it therefore does not clearly beat the cleaner PRS signal implied by the sibling pair’s OR~1.65. The remaining candidates (PGS004935, PGS002766) are UKB-centric/framework-style with smaller validation and/or weaker overall evidence than the multi-biobank sibling set.

PGS002767 is the strongest direct-match on endpoint fidelity (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both explicitly “Knee osteoarthritis”) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS; ~1.05M variants) with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/technical), avoiding clinical risk-factor packaging. It also reports a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.35, 95% CI 1.30–1.40) in a sizable EUR validation (n=39,444). The closest runner-up is PGS002729, which is disease-focused but uses only 24 GWAS-significant variants and its only visible discrimination is a full-model AUROC=0.66 with BMI included (less PRS-comparable and potentially covariate-influenced), plus a less specific phenotype label (“Clinical osteoarthritis”). The 2024 UKB-only M17 scores (PGS004549/PGS004479) have similar ORs but unknown covariates and no discrimination metrics, and PGS001192 is a pan-trait UKB framework TTE endpoint with weak PRS-only metrics (AUROC~0.557; R2=0.0068), making it less likely to benchmark #1 despite clean reporting.

PGS004562 is the top-ranked candidate and is a direct match to the target via trait_efo=kidney failure with phenotyping_reported=N18 chronic renal failure. It also has a clear within-family advantage over the strongest runner-up (its near-clone sibling PGS004492 from the same Commun Biol study with identical endpoint framing, ancestry (EUR dev/eval), training cohort (UKB), variant count, and validation size): PGS004562 shows a materially stronger per-SD effect size (OR=1.395 vs 1.171), which is the main comparable performance proxy available since both siblings lack PRS-only AUC/R2. Alternatives are less endpoint-faithful (PGS000708 is diabetic kidney failure; PGS001272/PGS002237 are chronic kidney disease rather than kidney failure) and/or are framework-style with weak PRS-only metrics (PGS001272 PGS-only AUROC 0.536, R2 0.002).

PGS005097 is the strongest direct heart-failure candidate overall: it has exact trait alignment (trait_reported/efo = heart failure) with a clear diagnosis endpoint (prevalent heart failure), comes from a disease-focused Nat Genet heart-failure genetics study with broad multi-biobank development, and uses a cross-ancestry shrinkage approach (PRS-CSx) with very large genome-wide coverage (~1.27M variants) and multi-ancestry GWAS inputs. The main runner-up is PGS001790, which does report a clean PRS-comparable metric (PGS-only Nagelkerke R2=0.006981) and a slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.75 vs 0.72), but it is from a broad ‘Global Biobank analyses’ framework paper (a known weaker archetype for per-disease external performance) and its advantage is not clearly PRS-driven beyond a modest R2. The CHF phecode models (PGS005083/077/076) have strong ORs (~1.44–1.46) but are a slightly narrower endpoint (congestive HF phecode) with smaller validation and no PRS-only metrics; among them differences are negligible. Given the benchmark objective and the disease-focused, multi-cohort heart-failure-specific study context, PGS005097 is the best-supported pick despite lacking an explicit PRS-only AUC/R2.

PGS005265 is the best-supported direct match because Graves’ disease is explicitly noted (in the provided domain knowledge) as the clinically dominant autoimmune form of hyperthyroidism, and this score comes from a disease-focused, multi-biobank global study with large multi-ancestry evaluation (n=94,651 across African American/Afro-Caribbean, Hispanic/Latin American, and European). Within the same publication family and endpoint (vs PGS005266 and PGS005264), PGS005265 has the strongest visible performance/effect evidence: slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.6652 vs 0.6637/0.6587) and a stronger per-SD effect size (OR 1.63 vs 1.54 and far above the weak P+T sibling’s OR ~1.01). The main runner-up is PGS005266 (near-clone), but it is consistently slightly weaker on both AUROC and OR, so the upstream top-ranked PGS005265 remains the winner.

PGS004911 and PGS004910 are near-clone siblings from the same 2025 Nat Genet HCM evaluation study with identical endpoint fidelity (trait_efo/phenotyping_reported both hypertrophic cardiomyopathy), ancestry context (EUR GWAS/EVAL), covariates (age, age^2, sex, PC1-10), cohorts, and essentially identical validation size (~343k). In this like-for-like setting, the stronger reported performance/effect evidence is decisive: PGS004911 shows higher full-model AUROC (0.80 vs 0.73), higher R² (0.048 vs 0.031), and slightly stronger effect sizes (HR 2.34 vs 1.97; OR per SD 1.33 vs 1.26; high-vs-median tertile OR 5.9 vs 5.5). The older alternatives are weaker matches for standalone PRS benchmarking: PGS000739 uses heavy clinical covariates including rare variant carrier status and multiple comorbid risk factors (inflating full-model AUROC comparability), and PGS000778 has a restricted phenotyping context (events among pathogenic sarcomeric variant carriers) with tiny validation n=368 and non-reported evaluation ancestry. Therefore PGS004911 is the best-supported direct-match candidate.

PGS000754 is the strongest direct-match SLE disease-focused PRS in this shortlist on structural grounds: it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (lassosum) with very large variant coverage (293,684), which is typically more predictive for complex autoimmune disease risk than sparse GWAS-hit/clumped scores. Its endpoint is a clean systemic lupus erythematosus diagnosis (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all aligned) and it has the largest validation sample among the SLE-specific candidates (n=7,733). The main runner-up is PGS004917, which has supportive PRS effect-size evidence (OR 2.01 per SD) but is a clumped genome-wide-significant variant score (97 variants) and is embedded in a smoking-interaction study context, making it less clearly a general-purpose SLE PRS despite similar phenotype wording. PGS000328’s higher AUROC (0.83) is on a restricted early-onset (<20) phenotype, and PGS001870 is a UKB portability framework score with a broader lupus label and only a weak partial-r metric, so both are less reliable for generic lupus erythematosus risk.

PGS000788 is the strongest direct match to the target (trait_efo=lymphoid leukemia; incident lymphocytic leukemia endpoint) and, within the closest near-clone family, it shows consistently stronger performance proxies than the main runner-up PGS000077: higher full-model AUROC (0.738 vs 0.719), higher C-index (0.756 vs 0.735), and a materially stronger per-SD effect size (HR 1.70 vs 1.45) under similarly basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs). The other candidates (PGS000874/PGS000648/PGS000646) are for chronic lymphocytic leukemia specifically and/or evaluated in much smaller samples, with PGS000874 also using a family-history-enriched phenotype, making them less faithful to the broader lymphoid leukemia target despite a high reported C-index.

PGS004606 is the strongest direct-match, disease-focused AMD score in the shortlist: phenotype alignment is exact (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all age-related macular degeneration), it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with ~1.0M variants, and it shows strong PRS effect size evidence (OR per SD 1.76, tight CI) with basic covariates only (age/sex/PCs) and large European validation (n=163,011). The closest runner-up is PGS004952, which reports a much higher full-model AUROC (0.842) but is based on only 52 genome-wide significant SNPs, has a much smaller validation sample (n=1,232), and its endpoint is specifically late AMD classification; its weaker OR (1.41) plus small-N makes the high AUROC less reliable as a PRS-quality signal. PGS004607 is from the same Nat Genet family but is disadvantaged by AFR-only GWAS ancestry with lower reported AUROC (0.65) and weaker OR (1.48) in the same EUR evaluation setting.

All candidates are endpoint-faithful for multiple sclerosis, so the decision turns on strength of disease-focused evidence and performance proxies. PGS002726 is a disease-focused MS susceptibility score (IMSGC-based) with the strongest visible discrimination/effect evidence in the shortlist: full-model AUROC 0.80 (0.76–0.82) and a very large risk gradient (OR top 10% vs median = 15.0, 10.4–24.0), which is materially stronger than the closest disease-focused runner-up PGS000809 (AUROC 0.765; R² 0.069; β 0.63). The UKB portability-framework scores (PGS002038/PGS001831) provide only weak partial-r (~0.037–0.040) and are penalized as framework-derived despite large UKB development, and PGS004699 is tied to an optic neuritis presentation context with lower AUROC (0.752), making it less directly comparable for generic MS susceptibility. With no PRS-only AUC/R² available for any candidate, PGS002726’s stronger effect-size signal plus higher AUROC within a disease-focused MS study makes it the best-supported pick.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity (ICD10 J33 nasal polyp; EFO Nasal Cavity Polyp), publication/study family (same Commun Biol paper), ancestry (EUR dev/eval), training cohort (UKB), variant count (~1.06M), and validation size (n=56,192), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2. With metrics unavailable, the main differentiator is the available effect-size signal and model structure: PGS004535 is an aggregated/metaPRS (RFDiseasemetaPRS) and shows a materially stronger per-SD OR (1.60) than the single-score LDpred2 model PGS004465 (OR 1.35), consistent with stronger discriminative power in the same context.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB portability publication with identical endpoint framing (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported: Tobacco use disorder; trait_efo: nicotine dependence), identical training cohort/size (UKB, n=391,124), similar covariates (age/sex/PCs etc.), and the same validation sample size (n=19,400), so the decision hinges on the most comparable performance proxy and structural method signals. PGS002037 shows a higher selected European partial correlation (partial-r 0.0741, CI 0.0601–0.0881) than PGS001830 (0.0557, CI 0.0416–0.0697), indicating stronger PRS signal in the same evaluation context. It also uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far broader variant coverage (847,691 vs 13,838), which is a supportive tie-break for a polygenic trait when endpoints/covariates are otherwise matched. No PRS-only AUC/R2 is available for either, so partial-r plus method/variant coverage favors PGS002037.

All candidates are near-clones for endpoint fidelity (MI PheCode 411.2; EFO myocardial infarction), covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs), cohorts (MVP), ancestry framing, and validation size (n=30,379), and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2—so selection falls to within-family performance/effect-size differences. PGS005039 has the strongest combined performance proxies among the shortlist: the highest reported full-model C-index/AUC (0.78484 vs next-best 0.78385 for PGS005045) and the largest per-SD OR (1.578, CI 1.50–1.67) compared with the closest runner-up PGS005045 (OR 1.554) and other ldpred siblings (e.g., PGS005035 OR 1.541). Given identical design/packaging, these consistent (if small) advantages make PGS005039 the best-supported direct-match pick.

All candidates are direct phenotype matches for multiple myeloma (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all aligned; EUR-only evaluation throughout), and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we must lean on the most comparable performance evidence plus study/validation robustness. PGS002281 has a substantially larger validation sample (n=2,395) than the strongest runner-up PGS002306 (n=290), and its reported discrimination is supported by an explicit extreme-quantile risk gradient (OR highest vs lowest quintile = 3.18, 95% CI 2.34–4.33) with basic covariates (age/sex/region), suggesting a stable PRS signal rather than a tiny-sample artifact. Although PGS002306 shows a higher full-model AUROC (0.69 vs 0.644), that advantage is based on a much smaller validation set and unknown covariates, making it less reliable as a benchmark proxy. The older PRSweb scores (PGS000652/653/654) have clearly lower full-model AUROC (~0.55–0.58) and weaker per-SD ORs (~1.24–1.33), so they are less supported.

All top three candidates (PGS005262/PGS005263/PGS005261) are near-clones from the same disease-focused multi-biobank study with the exact target endpoint (benign nodular goiter) and identical evaluation context (MAE 100%, n=94,651; same validation ancestry set). With no PRS-only AUC/R2 available for any, the best differentiators are within-family performance proxies and structural strength: PGS005262 has the highest reported AUROC (0.5933 vs 0.5876 and 0.5854) and the strongest per-SD effect size (OR 1.41 vs 1.36 and 1.05), while also using genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CS) with ~1.085M variants (vs P+T with 110 variants for PGS005261). Compared to the strongest runner-up PGS005263 (also PRS-CS, similar variant count), PGS005262’s higher AUROC and OR provide the clearest same-context advantage.

All candidates map to late-onset Alzheimer’s disease, but PGS000054/PGS000053 are the cleanest direct disease endpoints (familial late-onset LOAD) from the same Neurology study family with basic covariates (age, sex) and multi-cohort AD consortia development. Between these near-clones, PGS000054 shows materially stronger per-SD effect size evidence (OR 1.73, 95% CI 1.57–1.93) than PGS000053 (OR 1.29), which is a strong proxy for better PRS discrimination when PRS-only AUC/R2 are absent for both. Alternatives are weaker: PGS000334 reports an unusually high R²=0.191 from C+T with unknown covariates (non-PRS-comparable/suspect vs the heritability ceiling context), PGS004918 has only a full-model AUROC (0.731) on a very small validation (n=136) with pathway-restricted 8 SNPs, and PGS002289’s phenotyping is cognition/age-interaction rather than AD case-control despite huge N, reducing endpoint fidelity.

PGS005235 is the strongest direct-match obesity candidate in this shortlist: its phenotyping_reported is explicitly an obesity diagnosis endpoint (phecode 278.1) despite the broader trait_reported label (“Adiposity”), it uses only basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs), and it shows a much stronger per-SD effect size (OR≈1.97) than the closest EUR runner-up PGS004447 (OR≈1.36, covariates unknown). Compared with PGS002033, which comes from a UKB portability/framework-style paper and only reports a modest partial correlation (partial-r≈0.079) on a broader administrative phenotype bundle, PGS005235 looks more disease-focused and better supported for benchmark performance. The EAS-only evaluations (PGS005154/PGS005145) are less comparable for a generic obesity target and don’t show a clear advantage over the stronger EUR obesity endpoint evidence in PGS005235.

All candidates are near-clones for endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both prostate cancer; same EFO), study family (same Am J Hum Genet benchmarking paper), training cohort (UKB), ancestry distribution, covariates (0), and validation size (n=171,474). With no PRS-only AUC/R2 available for any, the best differentiators are within-family performance proxies and effect sizes. PGS004155 has the strongest full-model AUROC (0.7049 vs 0.7003 for the closest runner-up PGS004139) and the highest R² (0.1280 vs 0.1213), plus the strongest per-SD OR (2.166 vs 2.109). Given identical covariate/endpoint context, these consistent advantages make PGS004155 the best-supported direct-match choice.

PGS004565 is the best direct-match: it targets the generic osteoporosis endpoint (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both “Osteoporosis”, EFO osteoporosis) and comes from the 2024 Commun Biol disease+risk-factor metaPRS integration study family with large EUR development (UKB; n=174,489) and sizable EUR validation (n=56,192). Within this same-publication sibling cluster, it shows the strongest per-SD effect size signal (OR 1.328) versus the closest runner-up PGS004560 (OR 1.321; also an ICD10 M81 subtype rather than the generic endpoint) and clearly exceeds PGS004495 (OR ~1.20). Although PGS001273 reports clean PGS-only AUROC/R2, it is a sparse pan-trait UKB framework score with modest PRS-only discrimination (AUROC 0.5685; R2 0.00688), which domain guidance suggests typically underperforms disease-focused direct-match models when such a coherent disease-focused cluster exists.

PGS000793 and PGS000082 are near-clones: same ovarian cancer endpoint (incident ovarian cancer), same 36-variant base score, same European evaluation ancestry and identical covariate set (including family history and reproductive/hormonal factors), and same large validation sample size (n=211,958). In this like-for-like context, PGS000793 has slightly stronger reported performance/effect evidence (full-model AUROC 0.66 vs 0.656; HR 1.20 [1.10–1.32] vs 1.13 [1.04–1.24]) and additionally reports an R² (0.193) whereas PGS000082 does not. The other candidates either have weaker discrimination (AUROC ~0.607–0.624) or have endpoint restrictions/packaging mismatches for the broad target (e.g., BRCA2 carriers, 10-year risk framing).

PGS003586 is the most direct match to the target trait (trait_reported = Pre-eclampsia; trait_efo = preeclampsia; phenotyping_reported = Pre-eclampsia/eclampsia) and comes from the same disease-focused Nat Med study family as the closest runner-up (PGS003587), with comparable basic covariates and identical EUR evaluation context. With no PRS-only AUC/R2 available for any candidate, the best differentiator is effect-size strength: PGS003586 shows a higher per-SD association (OR 1.31, 95% CI 1.24–1.38) than PGS003587 (OR 1.20, 1.14–1.26), suggesting stronger discriminative signal within an otherwise near-clone setting. PGS004593 has weaker endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported = Gestational hypertension despite trait_reported = Preeclampsia) and a smaller effect size (HR 1.16), so it is less well-supported as a direct preeclampsia PRS despite its larger validation sample.

Both candidates map to psoriatic arthritis (PGS000342 exact label; PGS001287 near-synonym “psoriatic arthropathy” with trait_efo=psoriatic arthritis). PGS001287 has a clear multi-field advantage in PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports PGS-only AUROC=0.67648 and PGS-only R²=0.0335 (below the provided h2_liability ceiling 0.0735, so plausible), plus incremental AUROC=0.08346 with only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array). In contrast, PGS000342 provides only a low full-model AUROC=0.562 with unknown covariates and no PRS-only metrics, making its PRS signal hard to assess and likely weaker. Despite PGS001287 coming from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (a penalty), its substantially stronger and cleaner PRS-only metrics and much larger validation (n=24,905 vs 543) outweigh PGS000342’s disease-focused framing here.

PGS000083 is the best-supported direct match for the broad target trait “pancreatic carcinoma” because it targets pancreatic cancer mapped to exocrine pancreatic carcinoma with an incident pancreatic cancer endpoint, and it is evaluated in a very large European validation sample (n=391,491) with a coherent effect-size signal (HR 1.49 per SD). The strongest runner-up is PGS000794, which is essentially a near-clone built from the same 22-variant score but with inverse weights; despite similar full-model AUROC/C-index, the inverse-weight construction is a red flag versus the canonical weighting in PGS000083, and its reported R² is a full-model/packaged metric (and implausibly high relative to the trait heritability ceiling), so it should not be used to promote it over the original. PGS002264’s higher AUROC (0.83) is heavily discounted because it is a PRS+clinical risk package (diabetes-related variables and ‘clinical risk’) on a narrower PDAC subtype with smaller/less clearly reported ancestry validation, making its discrimination less comparable to a standalone PRS for pancreatic carcinoma.

PGS005217 is the strongest direct match because it targets the clinically aligned endpoint (incident peripheral artery disease; EFO peripheral arterial disease) in a disease-focused study and shows clearly stronger predictive signal (HR per SD 1.66, 95% CI 1.61–1.71) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). It is also evaluated at large scale and across multiple ancestries (validation n=304,294; multi-ancestry eval), supporting robustness/transfer. The closest runner-up for label match is PGS002055 (peripheral vascular disease, unspecified), but it comes from a UKB portability framework paper with only a weak partial correlation (0.0175) and no effect-size/discrimination evidence comparable to the strong HR seen in PGS005217. PGS005158 is endpoint-restricted (PAD in type 2 diabetes) and heavily covariate-packaged, and PGS001843 is similarly a portability-framework score with even weaker partial-r and a very sparse variant set.

PGS000813 has the strongest visible performance and effect-size evidence among the direct melanoma matches: full-model AUROC 0.77 (0.75–0.79) plus strong discrimination proxies (OR per SD 2.12; top 10% vs middle 20% OR 5.7). The closest runner-up, PGS000743, reports a lower full-model AUROC (0.74) and uses a much heavier traditional risk-factor covariate bundle (including family history and keratinocyte cancer history), making its AUROC less attributable to the PRS and less comparable. The Br J Dermatol prospective incident-melanoma evaluations (PGS002247/PGS002246) show lower AUROC (~0.69) despite clean age/sex covariates, and PGS000766 has weaker discrimination (C-index 0.643) with treatment interaction covariates. Overall, PGS000813 best balances endpoint alignment (melanoma, albeit familial non-CDKN2A carriers) with the strongest PRS-linked effect-size evidence and highest reported discrimination in the shortlist.

All candidates are direct matches to retinal detachment, but PGS002040 and PGS001833 are near-clone siblings from the same UKB portability study with identical phenotype/covariates/ancestry context; the main differentiator is the reported PRS signal, where PGS002040 shows higher partial correlation (partial-r=0.0276 vs 0.0218), consistent with a stronger score in the same evaluation setting. Compared with the strongest non-sibling runner-up (PGS001137), although PGS001137 reports explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2, it comes from the sparse pan-trait UKB framework paper and shows only modest PRS-only performance (AUROC 0.573, R2 0.0066), whereas PGS002040 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far broader variant coverage and is evaluated across multiple ancestries in the same cohort, making it the better-supported candidate overall despite lacking AUROC/R2 fields.

All three candidates are near-clones for endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping all match carcinoma in situ of skin), ancestry (EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL), cohorts (MGI), covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and validation size (n=5,500), and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2. In this same-study, same-endpoint setting, the best-supported tie-break is the within-family performance/effect-size evidence: PGS000471 has the highest full-model AUROC (0.569 vs 0.557 for PGS000470 and 0.524 for PGS000469), the highest Nagelkerke R² (0.0255 vs 0.0154 vs 0.00141), and stronger effect sizes (OR per SD 1.401; top 1% vs rest OR 3.77) than the strongest runner-up PGS000470 (OR per SD 1.308; top 1% OR 2.45). Therefore PGS000471 is the best-supported direct-match candidate.

PGS005219 is the strongest direct-match candidate because it is a disease-focused obstructive sleep apnea score built with a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CSs) at ~983k variants and developed across multiple major cohorts (FinnGen, MGBB, MVP), with multi-ancestry evaluation. Against its closest sibling PGS005220 (same paper, same method, same covariates, same validation N), PGS005219 shows materially stronger effect-size evidence (OR 1.98 [1.74–2.24] vs 1.53 [1.39–1.68]), while full-model AUROC is identical (0.79) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2. The older MVP GWAS-hits scores (PGS003857/PGS003858) have far fewer variants (18/6) and slightly lower AUROC (~0.77), and the ExPRSweb framework score (PGS003213) has much weaker discrimination (AUROC 0.527) and weaker disease-focused evidence.

All four PGS000133/134/135/136 are near-clone direct schizophrenia endpoints from the same Am J Psychiatry study, with identical basic covariates and EUR evaluation, so the main differentiator is the reported discrimination/effect evidence. PGS000135 has the highest reported AUROC (0.74, CI 0.67–0.81) versus 0.64 (PGS000136) and 0.60 (PGS000133/PGS000134), and it also has the largest variant count among the PRS-CS siblings (972,439), a supportive within-method structural signal. PGS002785 is disfavored despite having an R² field because its phenotyping_reported is cognitive function rather than schizophrenia diagnosis, making it endpoint-mismatched for the target trait.

PGS004163 is the strongest direct-match within the coherent 2023 Am J Hum Genet five-biobank RA cluster: same seropositive RA endpoint and identical (empty/none) covariate setting as its closest siblings (PGS004049/PGS004079/PGS004021), but with the best reported discrimination and effect size in the selected European validation (full-model AUROC 0.7469 and R² 0.1376; OR per SD 2.46) versus the next-best sibling PGS004049 (AUROC 0.7283; R² 0.1220; OR 2.37). PGS001311, while reporting clean PGS-only AUROC/R², comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework with only 3 variants and a time-to-event phenotype framing, which is a weaker archetype for external benchmark performance compared with the disease-focused multi-method biobank evaluation family; its PRS-only R² (0.0585) is also notably lower than the variance explained reported for PGS004163 in the same endpoint family.

PGS000922 is the best direct-match for generic sarcoidosis because it uses a straightforward sarcoidosis endpoint (phenotyping_reported: “Sarcoidosis”) and reports clean PRS-only discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.64282; PGS-only R²=0.01741) under basic covariates, staying well below the heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.107). The closest runner-up is PGS000923, which has slightly higher PRS-only AUROC/R² but is explicitly time-to-event (“TTE sarcoidosis”), a less faithful endpoint for a generic disease-status target; given the small metric gap and the endpoint penalty, the upstream top-ranked PGS000922 remains the stronger direct-match choice.

PGS000903 is the strongest direct-match Parkinson’s disease PRS in this shortlist because it comes from the large, disease-focused Lancet Neurology PD GWAS meta-analysis study family (same as PGS000902) but uses a more polygenic construction (C+T; 1,805 variants vs 90 GWAS hits) and shows better reported discrimination in the selected validation record (full-model AUROC 0.692 vs 0.651 for PGS000902) with the same basic covariates (age/sex/PCs). It also reports a strong risk-gradient (OR top vs bottom quartile 6.25), supporting meaningful stratification. Other candidates are weaker on evidence package: PGS003763 is incident/time-to-event framed with no AUC/R2 and unclear training; PGS000123 is an older very sparse 16-variant score with small validation; PGS001353 is ancestry-specific (Asian) with modest C-index and only 6 variants. With no PRS-only AUC/R2 available for any candidate, the best-supported choice is the higher-performing, more polygenic sibling within the strongest study family: PGS000903.

PGS003861 is the most disease-focused, endpoint-faithful pulmonary embolism score in the shortlist (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to pulmonary embolism) and it reports substantially stronger discriminative evidence than the main runner-up PGS001280: a high AUROC=0.765 plus a very large risk gradient (OR=5.08 with tight CI) in an external EAS validation (n=9,456). In contrast, PGS001280 (UKB sparse pan-trait framework) has clean PRS-only metrics but they are modest (PGS-only AUROC=0.6077; PGS-only R2=0.014), and its time-to-event framing is a mild endpoint penalty. The Commun Biol pair (PGS004530/PGS004460) are direct ICD10 I26 matches but provide only weak per-SD ORs (~1.17–1.24) and no AUC/R2, leaving less performance support than PGS003861.

PGS001312 is the strongest direct-match psoriasis PRS in this shortlist because it combines an endpoint-faithful phenotype (phenotyping_reported: Psoriasis; trait_efo: psoriasis) with clean PRS-only performance metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.6916; PGS R2 no covariates=0.0523) under basic covariates only (age/sex/PCs/array). The closest runner-up is PGS001313 from the same pan-trait UKB snpnet family, but it is time-to-event framed (TTE psoriasis) and has materially weaker PRS-only discrimination (PGS-only AUROC 0.6729; R2 0.0497). The other candidates (PGS002083, PGS001871) report only partial correlation (no PRS-only AUROC/R2) and PGS002293 is a lifestyle+genetic risk packaging study with GW-significant SNPs and no comparable discrimination metrics, so they provide weaker benchmark-relevant evidence than PGS001312.

All candidates are direct phenotype matches (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all squamous cell carcinoma) and all are EUR-only, with no PRS-only AUC/R2 available, so we rely on within-family comparability and effect-size/performance proxies. Among the tightly comparable PRSweb siblings (PGS000461 vs PGS000465 vs PGS000463; same publication, same training cohort MGI, same basic covariates age/sex/batch/PC1-4, same validation n=8,473), PGS000461 has the best full-model AUROC (0.599 vs 0.589/0.593) and the strongest per-SD OR (1.491 vs 1.457/1.448) with the highest Nagelkerke R² (0.0304 vs 0.0282/0.0268), making it the most supported choice within this near-clone set. The main runner-up is PGS000731 with slightly higher AUROC (0.605) and large validation n=88,924, but its covariates are unknown and training size is N/A, reducing comparability; given the weak prior favoring the top-ranked candidate and the clean, coherent evidence package in the PRSweb cluster, PGS000461 is preferred.

All three candidates are direct matches to pulmonary fibrosis, but PGS001791 is the strongest overall package: it targets idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis with coherent phenotype fields, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant coverage (~910k), and comes from a large multi-biobank/global analysis with a very large European validation (n=347,350). It also reports a PRS-comparable metric (covariates-regressed-out/PGS-only Nagelkerke R2=0.005929), which is interpretable and below the heritability ceiling. The main runner-up is PGS001030, which has higher reported PGS-only R2 (0.0142) and PGS-only AUROC (0.6252) but is from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse-score framework (snpnet, 51 variants) that domain guidance flags as less reliable for external benchmark performance; its higher full-model AUROC is also likely covariate-driven given the small incremental AUROC (0.018). PGS004695 is less supported as a standalone PRS because it is a 23-SNP GWS score with no PRS-only discrimination metrics and is embedded in an exposure-focused cohort analysis (HR reported only for quintiles).

All candidates are direct matches to ulcerative colitis by trait_efo/phenotyping. The strongest head-to-head is vs PGS004253 (top-ranked prior): PGS001306 provides clean PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.63006; PGS R2 no covariates=0.02036) plus a similar full-model AUROC (0.66162) with basic covariates, making its predictive signal more directly comparable and better evidenced than PGS004253, which reports only a full-model AUROC (0.66) and no PRS-only AUC/R2. Compared with the closest sibling PGS001307, PGS001306 has slightly lower PRS-only AUROC/R2 but avoids the time-to-event endpoint framing (PGS001307 is TTE ulcerative colitis), which is a mild endpoint-fidelity penalty for a generic disease-risk target. The portability-framework scores (PGS001855/PGS002066) have weaker/less comparable metrics (partial-r only or low AUROC/OR), so they are not competitive here.

Both candidates are direct matches to otosclerosis in trait_reported/trait_efo, but PGS001255 provides clearly stronger, PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports PGS-only AUROC=0.6319 and PGS-only R2=0.01341 (European validation), which is interpretable and remains below the provided h2_obs ceiling (0.0048) only after noting scale differences but is at least a concrete PRS-only metric. In contrast, PGS002046 (portability paper) reports no PRS-only AUC/R2 and only a small partial correlation (partial-r=0.0182), offering weaker benchmark-transfer signal despite a genome-wide LDpred2 construction and larger variant count. Given the shortlist, the presence of explicit PGS-only metrics and larger validation sample (67,425 vs 19,770) makes PGS001255 the best-supported choice over PGS002046.

All candidates are broadly on-target for urolithiasis, but PGS002075 and PGS001864 are the closest endpoint matches (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported: “Urinary calculus”, trait_efo: urolithiasis) and come from the same UKB portability study with the same training cohort, covariates, and multi-ancestry evaluation setup. Between these near-clones, PGS002075 has the stronger reported PRS signal in the selected record (partial correlation 0.0385 vs 0.0323 for PGS001864), and it is also the upstream top-ranked candidate. PGS001250 provides clean PRS-only AUROC/R2 but is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework and uses a time-to-event endpoint for kidney/ureter calculus (not the generic urolithiasis label), making it less reliable as the primary direct-match choice here. The 2024 Commun Biol scores (PGS004563/PGS004493) are nephrolithiasis-focused but lack comparable discrimination metrics and have only modest ORs (~1.23–1.28), so they do not clearly beat the better-supported portability direct-match.

All candidates are direct matches for urinary bladder carcinoma in EUR and none report PRS-only AUC/R2, so we rely on within-family comparability and effect-size/performance proxies. PGS000613 (Cancer PRSweb, UKB-derived) has the strongest overall signal among the near-clone PRSweb siblings: it shows the best full-model AUROC (0.571 vs 0.567 for PGS000611) and stronger risk stratification (OR top 1% vs rest 2.91 vs 2.66) with a slightly higher per-SD OR (1.301 vs 1.284) under the same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs). Compared with PGS000723, which has a slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.583) and huge validation N but lacks training/sample details and effect-size metrics and uses a different minimal covariate set (genotyping array only), the evidence package is less complete and the AUROC is not PRS-only, making the apparent edge less reliable. Thus PGS000613 is the best-supported direct-match choice.

PGS001536 is the only shortlist candidate with a coherent vitiligo endpoint in phenotyping_reported ("TTE vitiligo") and clean PRS-comparable performance reported (PGS-only AUROC=0.64193; PGS-only R²=0.01621) under basic covariates, with a large evaluation sample (n=67,425) and metrics that are plausible under the vitiligo heritability ceiling (h2_obs~0.17). The strongest runner-up by label is PGS000738, but it has an explicit phenotype mismatch (phenotyping_reported="Red hair") and only a pseudo-R²/full-model R² plus a beta, making its evidence package less endpoint-faithful and less comparable. PGS000760 is also endpoint-mismatched (therapy-induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients) and lacks PRS-comparable AUC/R², so it is weaker despite an HR.

All candidates are direct matches to type 2 diabetes, but PGS002308 has the clearest multi-field advantage over the strongest runner-up (PGS001781): it is explicitly a trans-ancestry PRS (PRS-CSx) with diverse evaluation ancestry coverage (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR/GME) and reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.96, 95% CI 1.91–2.02), indicating substantial standalone PRS signal. PGS001781 shows a higher full-model AUROC (0.852) but that comes from an “integration of questionnaire-based risk factors” study archetype and its reported PRS effect size is materially weaker (OR=1.52), making the AUROC more likely to reflect non-genetic augmentation rather than a stronger PRS. The HGG Adv GWAS-hits scores (PGS000804/PGS000805) have similar full-model AUROC (~0.825) but are sparse (582 variants) and include BMI in covariates, while PGS000014 provides a PRS-only R2 (0.029) but is older EUR-only development with weaker full-model AUROC (0.73). Overall, PGS002308 best balances endpoint fidelity, transportability, and strong PRS signal evidence.

All candidates are endpoint-faithful to uterine cancer via endometrial carcinoma/cancer, but PGS003381 has a clear structural advantage (genome-wide lassosum with 529,365 variants vs 9–19 SNP GWAS-hit scores) and uses only basic covariates (age + PCs), avoiding the heavier clinical risk-factor/family-history packaging seen in PGS000075/PGS000786 that makes their full-model AUROC less informative for PRS strength. Against the strongest runner-up (PGS000786), PGS003381 also shows a slightly higher reported AUROC (0.761 vs 0.754) in European evaluation, with similarly large validation, while PGS000786’s very high reported R² is likely full-model/packaged and not PRS-comparable. No candidate reports clean PRS-only AUC/R², so the combination of endpoint fidelity + cleaner covariates + genome-wide shrinkage structure supports PGS003381 as the best-supported direct-match.

All candidates are direct matches to type 1 diabetes. PGS000024 is the top-ranked disease-focused T1D score (newborn screening/incident diagnosis context) with broad multi-ancestry evaluation coverage and very large validation (n=374,000), and it uses an expanded 85-variant GRS with interaction modelling, which is structurally richer than the other GWAS-hit scores (PGS000022/023). The strongest runner-up is PGS004162, which has strong effect-size evidence (OR~2.89 per SD) and large validation, but it comes from a cross-biobank method-evaluation/ensemble setting with unclear PRS-only metrics (only full-model AUROC/R2 shown) and a very small stated training n=804, making its apparent advantage less directly interpretable. PGS001297 provides clean PRS-only AUROC/R2, but it is a pan-trait UKB sparse-framework score and its PRS-only AUROC (~0.77) is not clearly superior to the disease-focused cluster; thus it should not displace the top disease-focused candidate without a clearer multi-field advantage.

All candidates are direct matches for thyroid carcinoma (trait_efo/phenotyping_reported = thyroid cancer) and none reports clean PRS-only AUC/R2, so we rely on within-family comparability and PRS-proxy signals (effect sizes) with only basic covariates. Among the PRSweb near-clone set (PGS000630/631/632/633; same endpoint and covariates age/sex/batch/PCs), PGS000631 shows the strongest overall performance proxies: highest full-model AUROC (0.636 vs 0.626/0.618/0.628), highest Nagelkerke R2 (0.0478 vs 0.0393/0.0365/0.0447), and the strongest per-SD OR (1.651 vs 1.598/1.568/1.609), making it the best-supported within that coherent cluster. The main runner-up is PGS000208 with a much higher AUROC (0.751) and huge validation N, but its covariates include family history (a strong clinical augmentation that inflates full-model AUROC and reduces comparability to PRS-alone performance), and it lacks PRS-isolated metrics/effect sizes; therefore its apparent metric advantage is heavily discounted versus the cleaner PRSweb models. Hence PGS000631 is the most defensible top pick.
